premises: Coarse grains allow extended dislocation motion and crack-tip blunting, enhancing plastic strain and toughness at high temperature.
Fine grains restrict dislocation mobility, causing strain localization and reduced energy dissipation at the crack tip.
Grain boundaries act as sources/sinks for dislocations and regulate plastic deformation at the crack tip.
The proposed mechanism operates without changes in phase composition or secondary phases.
The trade-off between strength and toughness is governed by grain-boundary-mediated dislocation dynamics.
